title: Answer to Question: Regarding the Effect of the Economic Crises on the Fate of the Euro and the Fate of the European Union
text:
Answer to Question: Regarding the Effect of the Economic Crises on the Fate of the Euro and the Fate of the European Union

Question:

On the evening of 12/11/2011 Silvio Berlusconi, the Italian Prime Minister, announced his resignation, and three days before him, specifically on the evening of 9/11/2011, George Papandreou announced his resignation from the premiership of the Greek government, because of the financial and economic crisis sweeping their two countries, at the head of which is the sovereign debt crisis, and after the parliaments of their two countries ratified austerity measures and the placing of their two countries under the supervision of the International Monetary Fund and the European Commission to implement those measures, within what was called the European rescue plan. Beside the crises of these two countries, which have interacted in recent days, there are similar crises that have occurred in Ireland, Portugal and Spain, and they have been continuing for more than two years, to the extent that the sovereign debt crisis has begun to extend to France, which is one of the largest states of the eurozone just as it is one of the largest of the European Union. All these states that are witnessing the crises in a striking manner are located in the eurozone. The question is: what is the extent of the effect of these crises on the fate of the euro and on the survival of its zone, which comprises 17 states out of the 27 states within the European Union? Indeed, the question goes beyond that to the fate of the European Union as a whole?!

Then, does that have an effect on the positions of the other major powers, America, Russia and China, and on Britain, which is a member of the Union but is not in the eurozone?

Answer:

1- The Greek sovereign debt crisis has affected the eurozone because of the fear of Greece defaulting on the payment of its debts, which amount to about 350 billion euros, that is, the equivalent of 482 billion dollars. These debts exceed its domestic product by 160%, to the point that the deficit in its budget has reached 13.6%, with the knowledge that the level of deficit permitted at the European level is 3.5%. The European Commission and the International Monetary Fund asked Greece to apply austerity measures within the so-called European rescue plan, but Papandreou wanted to back away from applying more of them, so he called for holding a referendum on those measures, and 5 ministers in his government supported him, among them the finance minister. But he was compelled to give up the idea of holding the referendum after the Europeans summoned him to the French city of Cannes and warned him that his country would not obtain additional funds if he did not implement the austerity plan. On 11/10/2011 the international creditors agreed to disburse the sixth instalment to Greece, amounting to 8 billion euros. On 10/21/2011 the government approved more austerity measures, defying the demonstrators and the country's entry into a state of general paralysis as a result of a general strike and violent protests in Athens.

2- It is known that the beginning of recession and contraction in Europe was officially announced in November 2008, shortly after the eruption of the global financial crisis from its centre in America. Financial and economic crises then began to appear one after another: from the crisis of the stock markets and the collapse of companies and banks, and the attempt of states to rescue them by pumping enormous funds into their body, which formed a heavy burden on the states without treating the problem, to the extent that this was considered one of the causes of the sovereign debt crisis; that is, this treatment caused an increase in the disease and produced symptoms that are not only side effects but principal ones. The euro crisis emerged when its value began to fall against the main world currencies, especially the dollar. And the latest, though not the last, was the eruption of the sovereign debt crisis, that is, the crisis of the debts of states, which means that the income of the state and its domestic product are less than the debts owed by it, which it issues as treasury bonds. When the income of the state and its domestic product become less than the value of these debts, which are in the form of bonds, for numerous reasons, and which other states, banks and global financial institutions buy, then this state is counted as unable to pay its debts. So the value of the bonds falls, and the interest on them rises, as does the cost of insurance, so the public debt increases and confidence in these bonds disappears, and no one any longer comes forward to buy them; rather, people set about getting rid of them, because the state that issued the bonds is unable to pay them, so its deficit appears. In this way the crisis erupts, affecting the economy of the country as a whole, and indeed its political stability and the position of its governments. This is what happened with Italy recently, and it led to the fall of Berlusconi's government, just as it happened with Greece and led to the fall of Papandreou's government.

3- France and Germany are working to solve the problems of the eurozone, but it appears that there are disagreements between them that have been considered fundamental, on how to manage the crisis and how to treat it, and on whose proposal is to be accepted! Especially since the subject of the economy collides with the subject of the sovereignty of states. France and Germany consider themselves two great heads and two leaders of the European Union, so there is a hidden competition over sovereignty between them as to who is to be the holder of the decision and the holder of the word in this Union. Ulrike Guérot, head of the Berlin office of the European Council on Foreign Relations, expressed this on an earlier date in her words addressed to the states of the Union: "If you come from two completely different directions, you will certainly collide with one another. But I hope there will be a constructive dialogue." (Reuters 20/5/2011)

Thus the disagreement between France and Germany has appeared in the treatments put forward by each of them. France proposed the establishment of an economic government as a treatment for those crises, but Germany proposed the establishment of an economic administration concerned with creating structures and frameworks of work and imposing sanctions. It did not agree to the economic government, because it gives the impression that a higher body outside the will of the European governments dictates a particular economic policy to everyone, which means provoking the resentment of the other states that this diminishes their sovereignty. Therefore this proposal did not see the light. There is a difference over the subject of economic development: Germany carried out difficult adjustments to activate the export process, which cause imbalances in trade balances across Europe that cannot be borne, especially since Germany records large trade surpluses while the other states, among them France, show trade deficits of billions of euros. Therefore France asked Germany to strengthen domestic demand and reduce taxes to encourage imports, whereas Germany asks the other states to follow its example and demands that they reduce wages. Among the disagreements over the treatments also is the European Stability Fund and increasing support for it. Germany increased its share in it from 123 billion euros to 211 billion euros after the German parliament approved that on 29/9/2011. This indicates that Germany clings to the survival of the euro and is working for its continuation by supporting the states of its zone, made up of 17 states. The European states pledged to strengthen the Stability Pact, which is supposed to limit deficits but collapsed with the crisis. Among Germany's proposals is freezing financial support to states that allow the deficit in their budget to rise greatly. The European Commission considered it but saw that this does not solve the problem but rather keeps it. Germany also proposed freezing the voting rights of these states for a period of at least one year on the subject of decisions taken at the level of the European Union, which would disable the role of the states facing difficulties in the Union. Germany also proposed that the other states follow its example in setting a ceiling on the deficit in their constitutions, and in establishing procedures for declaring the bankruptcy of states that suffer from great indebtedness, which would have no option but to leave the eurozone...

However, these treatments require a change in the Lisbon Treaty, which governs the European Union and which came out after a difficult birth because of the sharp disagreement among the states of the Union, which work to keep sovereignty for themselves as independent states within the Union and are not prepared to make concessions for the interest of all. Therefore it is not easy to approve the German proposal. The latest German proposal was put forward by Germany's finance minister Wolfgang Schäuble when he called for "transferring more of the competences of domestic fiscal policy in the states of the eurozone to the European level to solve the sovereign debt crisis," as he pointed out that "the European Central Bank has an independence that qualifies it to pursue a policy that takes account of the interest of the whole, and that no state be favoured at the expense of the others." But he added, saying: "Until now no common European fiscal policy has been agreed." (DPA 12/11/2011) He acknowledged what Greece is facing and described it as "a mountain of problems." Previously there were statements by Angela Merkel, the Prime Minister of Germany, in which she warned about the future of the eurozone and affirmed that "Germany does not want any state to go bankrupt, because that means the bankruptcy of all." She repeated that anew on 14/11/2011, saying before a conference of her Christian Democratic party in the city of Leipzig: "Europe is living through the most difficult times since the Second World War... and if the euro fails, Europe will fail." This indicates the existence of anxieties towards the euro and towards the cohesion of the eurozone.

The multitude of the Germans' proposals and warnings, beside the increase in their support for the European Stability Fund and the agreement to raise the budget of this fund from 440 billion euros to a trillion euros, all of this indicates the extent of their concern to treat the problem and the extent of their keenness for the survival of the European monetary union, the euro, and for the preservation of the eurozone, and indeed for the continuation of the European Union. It is understood from this that Germany will not, in the foreseeable term, give up the euro, its zone and the European Union, with the knowledge that the euro is considered the secret of this Union's success, and its fall means the fall or failure of the Union.

4- On the other side, this crisis has given America the opportunity to exploit it: on one hand, to divert attention from its own troubled financial and economic situation and from its being, originally, the source of the crisis in the first place; and on the other hand, to shake the Europeans' confidence in their Union and in their currency, as it works to bring it down or make it fail together with its currency, the euro, in order to prevent Europe from having an international influence that competes with it, whether in the economy or in international politics. Rather, it wants to make it a follower of it, walking in its shadows. Therefore it works to help it to a certain degree so as to keep it a follower of it or to make it walk under its umbrella. At the G20 summit held at the beginning of this current month, America rejected proposals to double the funds of the International Monetary Fund in order to move towards solving the eurozone crisis. Its Treasury Secretary Timothy Geithner declared shortly before the meeting of the finance ministers of the G20 states: "He supports the Fund's support for Europe, but the latter has enough funds to solve its debt problems." And he said: "The United States is among the states keen to continue the pressure on the Europeans to take firmer measures to end the debt crisis that has been continuing for two years." (Al Jazeera 14/10/2011)

Moreover, the famous credit rating companies such as Standard & Poor's, Moody's and Fitch are American companies that play a role in shaking confidence in the financial situations of those states. They lowered their ratings for each of Spain, Portugal, Italy and Greece, and likewise Moody's on 7/10/2011 lowered its rating for a not inconsiderable number of European banks, numbering 21, among them major banks. The International Monetary Fund has estimated the losses of the European commercial banks from the euro crisis at about 200 billion euros since last year, in addition to losses in their assets estimated at about 100 billion euros. When the rating is reviewed, attention is also paid to the rise in unemployment in the country, which increases in direct proportion to the financial crisis, and to the rise in the indebtedness of the private sector and the deficit in the budget.

5- As for the position of Britain, which is a large member of the European Union, it stands in a corner on the edge of the Atlantic, from which it looks at the conditions of Europe, and it works to protect itself from the disasters of this Union and from the repercussions of the financial crisis that has struck it too. It does not want to take part in the solutions to the Union's problems so much as it looks for spoils and gains from it. It has not entered the eurozone, so it has not given up its currency and shows no desire to adopt it; so the matter of the euro does not concern it much. There are voices coming out of Britain calling for leaving the European Union, so that no one pressures it to adopt the euro or to integrate further into this Union. It has begun to "gloat" over the owners of the Union: its Foreign Secretary William Hague declared that "the euro will become a historic moment of collective folly," and he likened the eurozone to "a burning building with no exits," and he said that he was repeating his point of view that he expressed in 1998 when he was leader of the Conservative Party. And he said, inciting the Germans to give up the eurozone: "The Germans will have to provide support to the weaker member states such as Greece for the whole of their lives!" (BBC 28/9/2011) And the British Prime Minister David Cameron said: "The euro crisis poses a danger not only to the European economy but to the global economy as a whole." (BBC 2/10/2011) The politicians of Europe realise the extent of Britain's malice. José Manuel Barroso, President of the European Commission, pointed to that, saying: "The states of the Union that do not support joining the euro must not work to obstruct the states that want to advance along this path." (Al Jazeera 10/11/2011) Nevertheless, Britain does not intend to leave the European Union as long as it exists, because it works to achieve economic gains from it, beside political gains on the global scale, when it works to drag Europe into taking decisions that serve its interest. Indeed, leaving it would harm it, after it strove for long years until it managed to enter it. Therefore its Prime Minister Cameron declared, saying: "Britain's exit from the European Union does not serve its national interests. If we found ourselves outside the European Union, we would be in a situation similar to the situation of Norway, that is, we would be exposed to the effect of all the decisions that Brussels issues, but we would not be able to take part in making the decisions." (Russia's ITAR-TASS 14/11/2011) At the same time he refuses to give up British sovereignty, as he called for "handing over a large part of the powers of the European Commission in Brussels to the national governments." So Britain does not want to leave the European Union, and at the same time does not want to enter the euro system!

6- As for China and Russia, the survival of the euro is in their interest, in order to stand in the face of America, in the face of its dollar and its tyranny over the economy of the world. However, they do not do much for that, because the position of the eurozone, beside the position of the European Union as a whole, is not positive towards them. This zone and the Union still impose restrictions on them in their trade and economic movement, such as the movement of their traders and companies in Europe and the entry of their goods into it. For this reason they are not very enthusiastic about helping it. Therefore the Chinese President Hu Jintao, who attended the last G20 summit in Paris on the 3rd and 4th of the current month, did not indicate China's resolve to increase its investments in Europe and to buy the treasury bonds of the eurozone states, especially of the five struggling states, Italy, Greece, Portugal, Spain and Ireland; it bought a few of them to please Europe. Rather, its president Jintao said during his meeting with the French President Sarkozy on the sidelines of the G20 summit that "Europe ought to solve its crisis relying on itself." (Reuters 6/11/2011) By that he was indicating China's implicit refusal to support Europe, which had asked it, that is China, for support for the European Stability Fund, whose value it has raised to a trillion euros and which it is working to raise further than that. Whereas China supported the American economy by buying 1.14 trillion dollars of American treasury bonds, and it has bought more than a trillion dollars' worth of shares in American companies, and it has reserves of American currency amounting to 3.2 trillion dollars, as the statistics state. In return, America grants it great trade facilities. However, the political influence that America is able to exercise over it, making it support the American economy, this political influence is something Europe lacks towards China...

7- In the light of this, the European Union is under the weight of financial and economic crises because of the Capitalist system, and it is also under the threat of falling and disintegrating because of these continuing crises, which, when they occur in one place, do not strike its owners only, but their evil covers the whole inhabited world, because the whole world is tied into the network of the Capitalist system, under the weight of whose crises the people groan, suffering the two bitter things from the repercussions of these crises. This system cannot be reformed from within, because its basis is corrupt, so a sound economy cannot come out of it. Therefore it is obligatory to search outside it; indeed, it is obligatory to search for a correct system resting on a correct creed that agrees with the fitrah (innate nature) of man.

The world is in need of a system correct in its basis and its branches, and this can only be in the system laid down by the Creator of the universe, the Lord of the worlds, who knows what makes His creatures sound and makes them live a reassured economic life. Without this system, man remains anxious and wretched: "Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer. And whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed, he will have a depressed life."
